utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes. Good morning, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. In relation to Exhibit P2970, which was discussed on the 7th of July at transcript page 16291, a revised translation has been done and is uploaded and in e-court, and in relation to Exhibits P2990 and P2991, which were the log-books, the headings and the specific entries referred to, and this was discussed at transcript page 16330 to 16331, have been translated and have been uploaded and are in e-court. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Excellency. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As we broke off, we were discussing item 1, what you called your primary objectives, and item 2, the ideology of the Bosnian Serbs. Were you familiar with the programme and statute and documents, founding documents, the Serb Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In these documents, did you find what you call our ideology and our main objectives?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the statute and documents of the Serb Democratic Party that you refer to lay out the reasons for the founding of that party and its main objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So do you rely on that knowledge when you speak about -- about the ideology of the Bosnian Serbs and about our objectives? Is that what you have in mind, that programme?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I rely on is, among other things, those documents through the analysis of the report written by Pat Treanor, who was the main analyst engaged in an analysis of those documents. That is the context for which I used -- or which I used in preparing my report on the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that you dealt with or relied on reports of other experts in your own report, other Prosecution experts, that is?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have stated in previous testimony and as I believe I stated also last week, my report is one of a number of analytical reports produced by the leadership research team. Given the very large scope of topics that we were tasked to analyse, I was not able to analyse every single topic myself. I was tasked specifically to analyse the Bosnian Serb police and the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in doing so, I read the political analysis of the Bosnian Serb leadership produced by Patrick Treanor, and was informed by the political context that was included in that report. In many instances, I also read the primary sources on which Dr. Treanor based his own report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These papers, these -- this report of yours, are they expert findings of an expert witness?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the report that I have in front of me, and which the Court has in front of it, it is, as it indicates on the title, a research report that I personally and solely originally prepared for the case of Krajisnik. It was later updated for the Mico Stanisic case, and now also a corrected version was prepared for this case, and I regard this as an expert report, a research report, which forms the basis of my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm a bit perplexed, perhaps because I'm not a lawyer or because I don't come from that legal system. Let's try to spell this out in very specific terms. As an employee of the OTP, you investigated or explored the nature of the MUP of Republika Srpska, and you did not research the Presidency, the Crisis Staffs, the government. You did not investigate the behaviour of the second party and the third party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then you put all of your research together into this report on the basis of which you're testifying here now; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned just a moment ago, the topics that you just enunciated or listed are so enormous in scope that it would be beyond the capacity of any analyst, however capable, to deal with that on his or her own capabilities or capacities. That is why we had a leadership research team in the Office of the Prosecutor. That team was divided into research units, and we were each tasked to focus on specific aspects of, among other things, the Bosnian Serb leadership - other of my colleagues worked on, for example, the Bosnian Croat or Bosnian Muslim leadership - and I was in constant communication with other analysts on that team who would alert me, as I would alert them, to documents that were being collected and which might be potentially relevant for the preparation of their own reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that a witness has to be impartial by the very nature of things?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it is now that I find out that you are part of a bigger team that collected evidence about the responsibility of the Serb side in Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know now you just found out about this at this moment since it has been clearly indicated on my curriculum vitae that I was a member of the leadership research team of the Office of the Prosecutor. And I have in my previous testimony, as I'm sure you are aware, made it very clear that the methodology that I just described was the methodology employed by that team that I was a member of, of an analytical team focusing on readership research and that we collaborated internally in the manner that I just indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Nielsen. I just want to establish the capacity in which you're testifying here, as a researcher or as an expert, as an impartial expert witness, a professional who viewed everything that happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina, what everyone did, all the parties did, and then the Serb side within that context. Is it the first thing that I said, as a researcher?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a very important point. I was always during my employment at the OTP a research officer or analyst, those two being synonyms in the Office of the Prosecutor, and at no point during my employment for the Office of the Prosecutor was I an investigator. My primary task was to research and to analyse, not to investigate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So while you were doing that, your task was to collect as much relevant evidence as possible that indicates the responsibility of the Serb side; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I indicated last week, my task was to collect as much relevant evidence as possible about the functioning of the police and the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, how do I then treat those parts of your report that pertain to the SDS, to the Crisis Staffs, et cetera, when you did not explore that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as the Court has heard in the testimony of my former colleagues Dorothea Hanson and Patrick Treanor, who were also members of the leadership research team, we were all working on very complex topics, which as the Court I'm sure recognises, cannot always be neatly delimited. For example, in the case of a document in which the Crisis Staff and the police are co-operating, should that document be solely the object of analysis of someone doing analysis on the Crisis Staffs or should it solely be the object of someone doing analysis on the police? In some cases, indeed in most cases, that document would be analysed by both analysts, the one working on the Crisis Staffs and myself working on the police. So to answer your question, this report is written as part of a group of reports that is to be understood as an effort to provide the state of the art of research on various entities, institutions, parties, et cetera, functioning under the purview of the Bosnian Serb leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the point of view of the OTP; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your task? How was your task defined, your personal task, not the tax of the entire group?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task, based on my academic background as an historian, as someone who had done very large quantities of academic and archival research into the functioning of the police in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, was to come in, starting in June 2002 when I was hired, and write a report on the functioning of the police in Bosnia and Herzegovina, specifically the establishment of the Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs. At the time that I arrived at the OTP, there was no such report that was in existence, and my supervisor, Patrick Treanor, tasked me, based on my experience with police documentation to prepare a report that would present again the state of the art of what could be known about the Bosnian Serb police based on the documents in the possession of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. In addition to that, you mentioned that you relied on newspaper articles. How did you get a hold of them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the leadership research team there was also a group of analysts who specifically worked with newspapers and television news reports, what in the analytical business we call open sources. Those analysts would read the -- both the media that we were collecting, for example, newspapers such as "Glas" from Banja Luka from the 1990s, but would also monitor the news that was being produced contemporaneously in the former Yugoslavia that might be relevant to the former Yugoslavia and specifically to the work of this Tribunal, and from those analysts, and also from my own research, I would on occasion come across open-source articles which I deemed relevant and therefore cited in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you get to them technically speaking? How did you get access to those media sources?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases those news articles would be found in various government institutions when we collected documents there. I recall on some occasions in police or government archives in Republika Srpska we often sometimes consciously, sometimes inadvertently ended up collecting their own archives of old newspapers. In other cases, I directly went, for example, to the offices of "Glas" in Banja Luka and asked them whether it would be possible to receive access to their archives from the war. In some cases, private citizens, and indeed, also journalists approved the OTP and offered their own collections of old newspapers because they deemed they might be relevant for the OTP and for the Tribunal. And lastly, in some cases, increasingly with the capabilities that the internet offers us, very large quantities of open sources became available through the internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, when you testified in Mr. Krajisnik's case, you said that it was the OTP that had made this possible for you and that in the OTP, itself, you found many of these articles that were registered with ERN numbers; right? That is page -- page 14000, I think, 14000, June 2005.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct, and I view that as being consistent with my previous answer. We both had collections. The OTP, as you know, had existed for several years before I arrived in 2002, and in other cases, as I indicated previously in my testimony, when I -- or my colleagues as analysts identified gaps in these documents collections, we on occasion went to the field in pursuit of more documents that would be relevant to these document collections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the OTP supplied you with documents, with most of the texts that you used, and you -- did you work on the basis of what the OTP had offered to you? What did you do with the documents that speak in favour of the Bosnian Serbs? Were there such texts there too? Were there such documents, and what did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see at least three, four separate questions in that section, so I would start by saying, yes, the OTP had documents which I was able to use, archives of documents. And again, very often I, myself, augmented those collections by going out and had very good co-operation with the Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs who provided us with additional documentations -- documentation when we sought that, and as well as with other institutions of Republika Srpska. To your next questions, when we found documents -- well, perhaps you could be more specific. What do you mean, "speak in favour of the Bosnian Serbs"? I did not see it as my task to write a report that was in favour, whatever that may mean, or against the Bosnian Serbs but, rather, to write a report, the sole purpose of which was to explain to the Court how the Ministry of Internal Affairs had functioned in the period from November 1990 until the end of 1992 in its various permutations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for this way of obtaining documents, you did not mention that when you testified in Mr. Krajisnik's case. Isn't that right? You just confined yourself to what you received from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be very surprised if I had not, at some point during my testimony in the Krajisnik trial, specifically mentioned that, as I did last week and as I did in the Stanisic and Zupljanin case, that I was involved personally in the collection of documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to primary goals as you call them, primary goals, and Serb ideology. What does the programme of the Serb Democratic Party contain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we leave, it's about the leadership research team. Is there a team leader? You at one point in time you -- Mr. Patrick Treanor was your supervisor. So was there a team leader that was -- is chairing or leading the team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In the period that I worked for the leadership research team, the leader of that team was Patrick Treanor as the chief research officer, and all the of the reports I produced, both internal work product and research reports for trial, were supervised and edited by Patrick Treanor, as my supervisor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you said the supervisor supervised or edited the work of the researcher. So what's the relation like between the chief researcher and the researcher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honour, as I indicated, Dr. Treanor tasked me to write this report that we have in front of us today. He then proceeded to let me work for several months at such point where I had a -- what I felt was a rough draft of the report ready. I would submit it to Patrick Treanor, who would read the report in the manner of an academic advisor. We would then go through the report where he would ask questions such as what -- what needed to be clarified further. He would point out any ambiguities in the report, and basically, we would have a back and forth through various drafts of the report before the final version of the report was produced. At no point in time could I produce a report or circulate it, much less submit it as an expert report, without the approval of the chief research officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then what's the relation like between the chief researcher and Prosecutor or trial attorney or trial attorney, senior attorney or Prosecutor? Does he report to the Prosecutor as to his -- his research?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the time when I worked at the OTP, I believe that the chief research officer was reporting to the chief of investigations of the OTP, and in tasking -- if there came a point when the senior trial attorneys or other legal officers wished analysts working for the research leadership team to perform any analysis, then such requests would be directed through the chief research officer to the individual research officers, myself included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the research team, leadership research team, is part of investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time that I worked for the team it was part of investigations. It has subsequently, I believe, been moved to a section called OTP support teams.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wasn't going to interrupt Mr. Karadzic earlier, but he took the witness -- he cited page 14000 of the Krajisnik transcript, and just above the questions about the media reports, Mr. Nielsen said he undertook a series of missions as a research officers to obtain additional collections of documents pertaining to the RS MUP from archives in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So I draw Mr. Karadzic's attention to that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Witness, what I basically meant was newspaper articles, and you said that there were a great many of them in the OTP; right? And that the OTP provided these documents to you and these articles; right? We've agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask for precision in terminology here. No one provided documents to me. As an analyst and a research officer working for the OTP, I had access to the document collections of the OTP. I did my own searches. I did my own research, and I was the person who decided which document collections I wanted to review. I identified the document collections that were necessary and useful to review in consultation with the chief research officer, particularly when I was new here and I was not yet familiar with the scope of those document collections, and as I indicated previously, on occasion my colleague analysts would also point me in the direction of document collections, including those with open sources that would be relevant to my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please now identify what do you understand by the term "primary goals and the Serbs' ideology in Bosnia," and did you find any elements to that effect in the programme of the SDS which was adopted on the 12th of July, 1990, and confirmed in 1991, as a political programme, whereas back in 1990 it was a founding programme? And the one in 1991 was designed for implementing and carrying out power.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I recall it, the primary goal of the Bosnian Serbs in -- or I should rephrase that. The primary goal of the SDS, which regarded it as the legitimate representative of the Bosnian Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina, was to represent politically and to protect the interests of that community, that is of the Bosnian Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now in that context what were the goals and the ideology that you identified in items 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly as I recall it one of the goals associated with the political representation and protection of Bosnian Serb interests was to ensure that the Bosnian Serb community would continue to reside in a political entity or country in which the other Serb communities of Yugoslavia also resided. That is, to oppose any efforts to separate Bosnia and Herzegovina from other territories in socialist Yugoslavia in which Bosnian Serb -- in which Serbs resided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doctor, do you know that at that point the Party of Democratic Action advocated the preservation of Yugoslavia and that the Serb Democratic Party made no mention of any Serb territories or regions but, rather, spoke about Yugoslavia as a whole? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that's accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that that was a foundation for our coalition with the SDA when we tried to exert joint power?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert on the political situation during that period, but I believe that you're correct in stating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that Mr. Izetbegovic, in his welcoming speech, said that he was in favour of a federation, by which he meant a Yugoslav federation?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that speech, but as I mentioned last week, I do recall that Mr. Izetbegovic was present at the establishment of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then say that the ideology of the Serbian Democratic Party at the time of its founding, as well as during the elections in 1991, was confirmed as having the element of the preservation of Yugoslavia as a community of different peoples, market economy, parliamentary democracy, open society and the participation of Serbs and democratic responses to all the problems that might arise? Is that what was literally contained in our programme?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if that was literally contained in your programme, your memory of it is certainly better than mine, but to the best of my recollection and, again, noting once again that I'm not a political expert, that corresponds to my understanding of the Serbian Democratic Party ideology, as you say, at the time of its founding. I would point out that, as with any political party, the methods in which the ideology were implemented evolved over time in reaction to a changing political situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, in item 6 of your report, you say that you based your report on the analysis of the documents available provided by the police and army, which were the material of the political nature relating to the RS, but you then added that this was not an exhaustive analysis of all the documents between November 1990 -- all the events between November 1990 and the end of 1992. Therefore, you embarked on a political analysis of Republika Srpska through the analysis of the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. Paragraph 6 of the report indeed correctly states the ambit of the report of which I have spoken several times already this morning. I would rephrase your last sentence. I find it much more accurate to state that I embarked upon an analysis of the police of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska which at times required an analysis of the effects of the political and military situation on the police. As I note in paragraph 6, all of these topics are inter-related, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to state where one topic begins and the other topic ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you speak about the ideology of the Bosnian Serbs in paragraph 2, you say that the SDS constantly expressed dissatisfaction with the steps taken by the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat politicians on the SRBiH's path on independence and you then go on to say in paragraph 4: These multi-party elections led directly to a multi-party agreement on the distribution of posts within the MUP of the SRBiH. This process in time -- in turn eventually contributed to the breakdown of the SRBH MUP and contributed to the outbreak of armed conflict in BH. First of all, Dr. Nielsen, didn't we agree on Thursday that every constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina ensured proportionality attributed to each of the three communities in government authorities and in power?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the war in Slovenia and Croatia began in -- begin in the same way? That is to say, that first they had multi-party elections, then all those who were entitled had proportional participation in power?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert on the origins of the armed conflict in Slovenia and Croatia, but I believe that the general gist of your statement is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did Croatia ensure proportional participation for the Serbs in Croatia, and was that the cause of the war or was the war caused by Croatia's disenfranchising of the Serbs and by throwing them out of the constitution, and did the war in Slovenia was caused by unilateral cessation from Yugoslavia? How do you compare that to the causes of the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that is a question to which I can only respond as a -- as a historian, as a specialist on the Balkans and not as research officer, because it is not a topic in which I engaged in research while employed by this Tribunal. I would agree that from the perspective of the Serb minority in Croatia, they believed that the Croatian Democratic Union, led by Franjo Tudjman, was engaged in a disenfranchising of the Serbs, and I agree that that contributed to a severe deterioration of inter-ethnic relations to Croatia. As for whether the war in Slovenia was caused by unilateral cessation from Yugoslavia, I believe that is a question best left to experts in constitutional law, of which I'm not one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then in item 5 you say that this report attempts to describe the de jure and the de facto structures of the MUP of Republika Srpska and the command-and-control relationships among the Bosnian Serb military police and the SDS in 1992. Then the report addresses the co-operation among the MUP, the army, the government, et cetera, and it depicts the deterioration and final break-up between these three organisations. Did you know that the Serbian Democratic Party put its work on hold throughout the whole of 1992? President Djeric demanded that the Serb Democratic Party put their dealings on ice and to suspend all activities.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said in item 6 that you did not provide an exhaustive analysis of all aspects. Which specific aspects did you disregard or you didn't take into account at all, and what was the basis for selecting them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I have in large part already responded to that question. With regard to the basis for selecting documentation, my first priority as an analyst was to read as many documents produced by the joint Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the period from 1990 until the beginning of the war in April 1992. After April 1992 and, indeed, also for the period immediately leading up to April 1992, I attempted to read as many documents as possible that were produced by Bosnian Serbs working in the joint police until April 1992 or in the organs of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska after April 1992. As such, this document, like any research report, is a living document. It is one that reflects the state of analytical knowledge of its primary topic, the police, at a given point in time, and it was augmented when new document collections became available, which led to the discovery of documents that shed light on salient topics dealt with in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In item 3, you speak about the fact that the SDS and Bosnian Serbs in MUP frequently asserted that the presence of Croatian/Muslim extremism along with increased calls for increased professionalism in the ministry was part of a cautious strategy. As in the overall political scene, the Bosnian Serbs in the MUP held to the perception that they were the sole preservers of integrity in policing and the real defenders of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Yugoslavia. Do you agree that the Bosnian Muslim and Croat extremism did exist in the police ranks?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you define extremism?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I was expecting you to tell me that, but let's move on. Do you agree that there was also lack -- total lack of professionalism in the Bosnian police?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that I would agree with a characterization of the Bosnian police as having a total lack of professionalism. What I do speak of in the report is a very high degree of politicisation of the police which grew from November 1990 until April 1992 and which brought forth very acrimonious accusations on all three sides that professionalism was not being adhered to in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 3 suggested the Serbs had a predesigned strategy or conscious strategy. You said that it was not necessary for the Serb representatives in the police to be members of the SDS. Now, what about Vitomir Zepinic, Momcilo Mandic, Slavko Draskovic, Tomislav Kovac, Boban Kosarac [phoen]; chief of CSBs such as Zupljanin, Bjelosevic, Goran Zugic, Stojanovic in Gorazde, were they all members of the SDS? Was any of these prominent police officials a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that any of them were members of the SDS. As I state in the report, it was not a requirement from the point of view of the SDS that their representatives in the police be members of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you agree that they had been in the police before that because they were professionally oriented in that way? They were lawyers, and they were trained to do their job. They had not been brought from somewhere else. They had already been working in the police.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the professional backgrounds of every single person you mentioned in your previous question. However, for those persons such as Zepinic, Zupljanin, Bjelosevic, with whom I am very familiar, I agree with you that they were in the police prior to the November 1990 elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Alija Delimustafic was in the SDA such as -- like Selmo --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please slowly speak the names of the officials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you name the names of individuals, please, you need to slow down, please. So could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to enumerate the names of the people who held highest positions in the police of Bosnia-Herzegovina and were members of the SDS [as interpreted] and had not been in the police previously but only joined the police after the elections. Alija Delimustafic, salesman, a member of the SDA, and used to be an ordinary policeman before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that Delimustafic was a businessman and that he had, a long time ago, been an ordinary police officer, but I do not know whether he was a member of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you say SDS or SDA at line 11?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I said SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Hilmo Selimovic came from the brewery and became chief of personnel and that he was at the same time a highly positioned official in the SDA?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the interests of time, I might as well point out right away that I'm not sure which high-ranking Bosnian Muslims in the joint MUP were actually members of the SDA as to merely being appointed and supported by the SDA, just as I'm not sure of that relationship between the SDS and the Bosnian Serbs for all cases, and likewise, I'm not sure of the exact relationship between the HDZ and the Bosnian Croats who were appointed at that time in the joint MUP. That is to say, I know that those persons were appointed with the support of those three parties, but I do not have information as to whether each of those individuals was a respect -- was a member of his respective party, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me simplify things for you. You observed that the Serbs' objection was that unprofessional and untrained and even criminal people be brought into the police ranks by the Muslims. That's one point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Secondly, that the joint police was being abused for the preparation of a republican army by arming the Muslims for a war against the Serbs, the army, and Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That is an allegation made by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that respect do you recall that Mirsad Srebrenkovic was a hodza, a cleric, and that the SDA recruited them to work in the police, in the personnel department, after Hilmo Selimovic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know into Mirsad Srebrenkovic was a hodza but I am familiar with the profound dissatisfaction of Bosnian Serbs in the joint police with his appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the name of Hasan Cengic and what his position in the SDA was?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Cengic was one of the highest functionaries of the SDA during this period. I do not know what his precise function was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the previous question and answer I don't think Mr. Karadzic said Mr. Selimovic was a hodza. His successor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mirsad Srebrenkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, I believe I misspoke. It's Mirsad Srebrenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Hasan Cengic was a hodza as well?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with these names: Bakir Alispahic, Munir Alibabic, Irfan Ljevakovic, et cetera? Do you agree that these people had been in the MUP previously and retained their highest position in the MUP after the multi-party elections?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the names Bakir Alispahic, and Munir Alibabic. Irfan Lakovic, I am not familiar with, but I do know that Munir Alibabic continued to work after November 1990 in the State Security Service as he had done before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please now look at 1D -- just one moment, please. 1D3886. This is a document. I don't know if there are restrictions regarding its being broadcast. I don't think there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to go into private session, and the document needs to be taken off the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure we have broadcast this. Do we need to go into private session right now? Yes, let's go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this document under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1516, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, do these names ring any bells, Senad Sahinpasic, Saja? Do you know that he was a prominent representative of the SDA, the owner of the newspaper "Vox," known for anti-Serb propaganda? He was also a businessman and he was also involved in the work of the joint police, of course. Please look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You need to repeat the names.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Senad Sahinpasic, Saja. You can see his name underlined or encircled, rather. Hasan Cengic; Senad Sahinpasic, Saja; Bakir Alispahic. The names do ring a bell, don't they.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with Hasan Cengic and Bakir Alispahic. I am not familiar with Senad Sahinpasic, Saja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go to page 5. This is research done by the institutions mentioned at the bottom, and the date is 8 June. Can we then go to page 6. There's a reference to the smuggling of a large number of passports providing extremists from the Far East with these passports. Look at the name. Omer Behmen. Are you familiar with his name?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that he had been imprisoned from 1939 [as interpreted] to 1983? He spent several stretches in prison. Finally he ended up as an ambassador in Iran. He was a member of the Young Bosnia Movement?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that Mr. Behmen was imprisoned the entire period from 1939 to 1983, but I know that he was imprisoned for his involvement in the Young Muslim Movement. He was one of a number of Bosnian Muslims, including Alija Izetbegovic, who was arrested for activities related to Muslim nationalism in socialist Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to page 7 or perhaps this has been enough. Can we then conclude that you're familiar with all these names and that these people were either among the top echelons of the SDA or highly positioned officials in the joint police; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we show another very similar document, D1180. It shouldn't be broadcast though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this document we have to go into private session if Mr. Karadzic wants to discuss it. It's under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I wouldn't be mentioning any sources. I would like to deal with the names mentioned in the document, that's all. I will not mention any sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could remind us, Ms. Sutherland, if it is okay if we do not broadcast this document and does not name the source.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I read the transcript of when this document was admitted, it was discussed in private session so, out of an abundance of caution, I would ask to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not yet. Let's go into private session. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document was discussed at transcript pages 13602 to 13607, and it was dealt with in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We are now back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the light of what you have just said, if that was the first step, then the removal of Bakir Alispahic and others from the police was actually the result of step one; right? They left the police under the pressure of the international community due to their links with the Muslim terrorism; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to state that that is the reason why Bakir Alispahic and the others were removed from the police. I know that in some cases it was because of concerns with their links with Islamic fundamentalists. In some cases it was due to a dissatisfaction on the part of the international community with the way in which they were releasing allegedly confidential information to the Bosnian media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now in that light again, in the light of what we have just seen, do you accept the fact that the Serbian side in Bosnia and Herzegovina and its representatives in the joint police had enough arguments and reasons to be concerned about the unlawful activities that were taking place in the joint police? Would you say yes or no to that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated in my report, the Serbian side in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and specifically its representatives in the joint police, definitely felt that both Croats and Muslims were undertaking nationalist, extremist or unlawful activities that were subverting the functioning of the joint police. In my report and in my testimony, I leave it merely at that, that is to say, I am merely stating that is what the Bosnian Serbs felt. I'm not making any statements about whether I agree with the accuracy of those assertions. I would also point out that in my previous testimony, I have on numerous occasions indicated that all three sides in the joint MUP in the period from November 1990 to April 1992 were engaged in activities which were detrimental to the functioning of a joint ministry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I note the time. Should I continue, or should we go on our first break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it is convenient. We will have a break now for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, in your report from paragraph 10 to paragraph 13 and further on, actually, you say that Goran Zecevic, as a Serb who used to work in the police, wrote a letter in which he is warning that there were irregularities in the police and that these irregularities are threatening the safety and security of one ethnic community; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that others wrote to me or to Ms. Plavsic as president of the council for constitutional order? People who were not members of the SDS, but they did write saying that the Serb side had -- had not actually paid much attention to the irregularities that were prevalent in the police.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I am quite certain that many other people wrote letters with content similar to that of the letter of Goran Zecevic. Unfortunately, I did not read many of those letters. Zecevic's letter was found in the archives of the SDS. We did not find many other such letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. -- Dr. Nielsen, I note that you are following B/C/S directly. In that case, please put a pause between question and answer. So the first part of your answer was not translated because of that overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. The first part of my answer was that I am certain that many other persons besides Goran Zecevic wrote letters with content similar to that of his letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, you did note, and you say that in paragraph 11, that Stojan Zupljanin noted that in his centre, in his security centre, persons were being appoint -- appointed without him knowing about it and without receiving proper clearance, and he said that he wrote about that to Ms. Biljana Plavsic who was ex officio president for the council for protecting the constitutional order; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you observed that -- actually, you're saying that in paragraph 15. Karadzic told Zepinic that basically the percentage of employed Serbs is not really important. If Serbs were even 90 per cent, they could not be a match to the others because they abide by the law whereas the others do not; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you do agree that I was not exerting pressure on them but that people from the grassroots were writing to me and explaining all of this to me, everyone except Zepinic, that Serb personnel in the MUP had been marginalised; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Serb personnel in the police and Serb personnel on the ground. From the police headquarters and from a grassroots level, they wrote to me saying that things were not moving in a good direction, and they were asking me to make sure that the power-sharing system that had been agreed upon among the political parties be followed and that I should exercise my influence with Kljuic and Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now start your answer again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apologies again. I agree that a number of Serbs in MUP, as well as Serbs outside of MUP, addressed grievances about the functioning of the police and in particular what they perceived to be the marginalised position of Serbs in the police to the SDS. The SDS, for its part, as I note in paragraph 14 of my report, had by the end of May 1991, decided that personnel decisions affecting Serbs in MUP had to be taken by the SDS centre, that is, the Main Board in order that these grievances could be addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree that that was part of the agreement among the coalition partners, the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ? And if things were not moving in the right direction on the ground, that had to be resolved between myself, Izetbegovic, and Kljuic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at paragraph 12 -- 20 of your statement where you say that Zecevic wrote to SDS council, Zupljanin to Biljana Plavsic and that Zupljanin claimed that Avdo Hebib, Hilmo Selimovic and so on and so forth were conspiring to form a purely Muslim army out of the police, and then you say Zupljanin said that Hebib and Selimovic insisted that 400 new candidates be employed of whom 80 per cent came from Sandzak. Zupljanin attached the statement of a brother by a Muslim police officer who claimed that, exacerbating the situation, Muslims were being spent to receive training in Croatia. I'm a bit perplexed. How can the situation be exacerbated by reporting? Is that really what you meant, that Zupljanin is making the situation worse because he's reporting on it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me answer the first part of the question first. What we see in paragraph 20 is a phenomenon where the Bosnian Serbs, from their perspective, are very concerned about what they regard as an inundation of the joint MUP with new employees of Muslim nationality, most of whom allegedly stem from the Sandzak. By contrast, at the same time, Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats were very concerned, and that's addressed elsewhere in paragraph 20, that they would be inundated by police who had -- particularly of Serb nationality who had formerly been in the Croatian MUP but who had now been either resigned their posts or been removed from service because of the deteriorating situation in Croatia. So on all sides there are mutual recriminations about manipulations with personnel policy along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to draw your attention, as well as the attention of all the other participants to the footnote number 33. I hope it's on page 21 in both languages. You say in June 1991, rumour circulated that Muslims were training in Croatia and also participating in combat actions against Serbs in Croatia. These rumours were proven false as it was clarified that the Muslim police officers were present in Croatia as a part of routine training. Nonetheless, the rumours served a propagandist purpose for the SDS. Is that correct? What was your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see what it is that is going on there, when the SDA is sending only Muslims to be trained in Croatia? D362. Can we have a brief look at that, please. So this is a document dated the 25th of July, 1991, and it is stated here that persons were being sent to the MUP of Croatia from Banja Luka for training. In Croatia there is already a situation of imminent threat of war; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe as of the 25th of July, 1991, it was not only an imminent threat of war, there actually was warfare in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Fighting was already underway, actually. So please have a look at this document. This policeman is providing information to the effect that he had learned from a fair Muslim who was concerned, worried, I don't want to mention his name now. It says he's a member of the SDA, and he said what is being organised here is that ethnic Muslims are being taken to the MUP of Croatia and that there is this training organised in Zagreb and that they are receiving a salary of 6.500 dinars. This is being financed by the United Emirates. They're getting uniforms and they're given questionnaires. They're supposed to fill them out. Did you know about all this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you thought that this was propaganda; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not what I state in footnote 33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But this is the official note you cited in footnote 33, written by Vojislav Pecanac.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This is indeed the document that I cite in footnote 33. However, what I refer to in footnote 33 is that accumulatively of all the documents I was able to review, it does not confirm the conclusion that these persons of Muslim nationality who were sent to receive training in Croatia also participated in combat actions. It states that they were sent to receive training, not that they participated in combat actions. So that's what I was referring to as an, if you will, as a propagandistic conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But rumours that Muslims were training in Croatia were proven true. Is that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. It is clear that some Bosnian Muslims did go to Croatia during this period and did receive training, among other ways through the services of the Croatian Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Do you know what they did after they got that training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know in all cases what these individuals did. There were many hundreds of individuals. I know from some documents that it is alleged that they returned to Bosnia and Herzegovina where they were allegedly involved in forming armed formations that were affiliated with the SDA or the HDZ. In some cases they may have remained on the territory of Croatia, but it is not a topic on which -- which I studied in detail, what happened with these people after they finished training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. D367. Can we have a look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Dr. Nielsen, do you agree that whenever people were employed in the police force they had to receive a proper clearance and it had to be checked, I mean, whether they had a criminal record or something like that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was certainly part of the normal procedure for obtaining employment in the police up until that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document in which Stojan Zupljanin is protesting because the following persons were employed and assigned to the Prijedor SJB, Ilijas Aliskovic, Omer Avdic, Muharem Ramic, et cetera. It says that Ilijas will go to Sanski Most, also that they were checked, their records were checked, and it says here with regard to the other employees from whom I had not provided a recommendation for employment in the MUP, they were being received nevertheless. You see what is happening. These people are being admitted in the police. They are employed without receiving proper clearance and without the chief of the centre knowing about it or giving his approval and it's not only that the ethnic structure is being changed, but also the moral and criminal structure as such, because if people who are not eligible to work in the police are being employed, that is what happens, if people who start working for the police who should not have been cleared in the first place. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, and there were a number of such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. D359. Can we have a look at that briefly. Do you agree that on the 31st of March, a decision was made to establish the Patriotic League? It was established on the 30th of April, and then on the 10th of June -- or, rather, the 11th of June the Council for National Defence of the SDA was established.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert on Bosnian Muslim structures or on the SDA, but based on my general recollection of events, what you just stated corresponds to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This has already been admitted, this document, and it is a document in which Hasan Cengic is informing the members of the SDA that this National Defence Council of the SDA has been established. 1D3854. Could we have that now, please. Actually, this happened on the 13th of June; right? On the 11th it was actually established, and information about that was provided on the 13th; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have 1D3854. Do you agree, Dr. Nielsen, that there is a list here, a list of persons who on the 20th of June were allowed to go home during the holidays? That is to say, they arrived before the 20th of June, and already on the 20th of June they're going home for a few days. The Secondary School of Internal Affairs, the sixth course for policemen, Zagreb, the 20th of June, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about how long or for what period of time these persons stayed at the police course in Zagreb, but you are correct. This is a document showing a list of attendees who are being allowed to go on home leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have page 2, please, in English. Can we focus on the municipalities that they come from, Jajce, Cazin, Doboj, Gracanica and so on? Are all of them Muslims? You're familiar with our names. Are all of these names Muslim?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The names you just mentioned are place names not personal names, but I agree that -- this list is a list of Muslims who it appears come from municipalities in various locations in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, in English we have a description of the 1st Battalion of the 2nd Company. All of them are Muslims too. Can we have in Serbian and in English the next page. There are 48 of them here who are going on leave; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have something different in English? We need the entire list. One page up in English. Page 1, actually. Page 1 in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid we do not have full translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 1 there is a translation of the entire list. That's the way it should be. Page 1 in e-court. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We have the 2nd Battalion somewhere as well with 28 names. I don't know where that is. If we go on leafing through this, we can find it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion. We've already seen that. Can we have the 2nd Battalion or, rather, the next page. All of them are Muslims, too; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it would appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note that the translation, English translation -- page 2 is the translation of this page, page 3 of B/C/S, where they have some handwriting, 2nd Battalion. I don't think we need translation as far as these names are concerned. Ms. Sutherland, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can admit this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1517, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3853. Could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the Party of Democratic Action and, et cetera, stamp? And it's already July, the 8th of July. Hasan Cengic, secretary. That's his signature; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this is a document of the SDA, a list of candidates for Special Police training at the MUP of the Republic of Croatia. I'm not sufficiently familiar with Mr. Cengic's signature to be able to say with certainty that that is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we please look at the next page. Look towards the end. Three sons of Islam Basovic from the same address at Ilidza. So the three of them come from Ilidza, and if we go through the list we can find 19 people from Ilidza in this group alone. Can we please now move two pages forward. We see Gorazde, and then 16 men from Nevesinje. Next page, please. Vlasenica. Yes, yes, Vlasenica. Look on this page, 26. Next page, please. Thirty-four, 31, plus three on the next page from Vlasenica. Do you agree, Dr. Nielsen, that according to the norms and rules in force at the time, if you had 34 Muslim policemen in Vlasenica police station, there was no place for a single Serb there.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot, off the top of my head, recall what the individual allocation of police officers was for any given municipal police station at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But Vlasenica had a total of 23.000 and 34 Muslim policemen. Now, let us look at the next page and Ilijas. The number of policemen in Ilijas envisaged is 18 Muslim policemen. Can we now look at the next page. Now, look at Visegrad. How many Visegrad should have? Twenty-five policemen from Visegrad. Now look at the seventh line from the bottom. Are you familiar with the name of Murat Sabanovic of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a man wanted to blow up the dam of the hydroelectric power plant in Visegrad and that his name was Murat Sabanovic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that in both Vlasenica and Visegrad, some bloody events took place, as well as in Ilijas and in all other places where these fake policemen came back from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it seems to me that any answer to that question first requires a specification of -- of time. When -- when did these bloody events allegedly take place? Second of all, I see here that people are being sent to Croatia to receive special police training. I cannot, a priori, reach the conclusion that sending people to receive police training makes them fake policemen, nor do I have any indication that the people listed on this very long list of names actually, in fact, went and received such training or completed such training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, do you know that none of those men was in the police? It was only planned for them to be in the police or in the armed forces, as you yourself put it.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the names on this list and therefore cannot conclude whether these are people who at the time of the writing of this document were or were not employed by the police in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page so that we can see how many men came from Srebrenica. Only in this group alone there were 23 of them from Srebrenica. None of them was a police officer. Here it is, Srebrenica, and it goes on on the following page. Thank you. Can we now have the last page. Four hundred and eighty-four, inclusive. That's handwritten. And it says the continuation of this list would be provided within seven days. Rasim Muharemovic, Sarajevo. Do you find that in a common state where the three peoples are sharing everyday life, the SDA is sending its members to be trained in Croatia where a war against Serbs had already started? What did this party have to do with this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I believe that I have indicated previously, there were many things ongoing in this period certainly on the Bosnian Muslim side, certainly also on the Bosnian Croat side, and also on the Bosnian Serb side, which were irregular and according to the allegations of their -- of their opponents, as it were, in the MUP were also allegedly illegal. This is a period when there were Croats who were apparently receiving police training in Croatia. Here we have an incident or a case, rather, of police of Bosnian Muslim nationality who are being sent to receive Special Police training in Croatia, and during this period, as I discuss elsewhere in my report, there were also persons of Serb nationality who were undergoing Special Police training in Pancevo, north of Belgrade. So a lot of training was going on during this period, and a significant amount of it, based on the records of the ministry itself, was taking place in -- along irregular lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find anywhere that the SDS was sending either the present or the future policemen anywhere for training?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of any documentation that shows that the SDS was specifically was sending future policemen for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1518, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D360, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All the pages are the same. We see here the instructions for candidate the SDA is sending to Croatia. Pursuant to all joint agreement authorise the representatives of the MUP of the SR B and H and the MUP of the Republic of Serbia -- Republic of Croatia, which is not true. Is that Hasan Cengic at the bottom and is the date the 11th of July when they promised to send as a continuation of the former list? Can we go through all the pages because these are identical texts. Only the names are different. There's a whole set of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that this document has been already admitted, do you need to go through it with this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Just to -- to leaf through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And my question is: Did you know that this was the way in which the SDA was sending their people to be trained in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was familiar with the fact that the SDA was sending -- or, rather, nominating people to be trained -- to receive police training in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3852, please. Let's see what happened with those people once they returned to Bosnia. 1D3852. I'm afraid that's not the right document. I think the number is wrong. ERN is 17796.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not catch the whole number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3852. Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here in Bratunac the chief of the public security station, Senad Hodzic, a Muslim, a professional and a responsible person, says that the number of reserve police officers has been increased by 100 per cent. That is paragraph 1. And then it says that they asked the Secretariat for National Defence to give them the surplus of conscripts so that they can recruit them as reserve policemen. That was on the 16th of March. "After receiving the requested list and started making inspected checks we obtained information that the list included a certain number of Muslim military conscripts who have spent time in Croatia on a part of the training of the MUP in Croatia. We do not know on whose orders or recommendation, but it is believed that Serbian citizens do not have enough trust in such future members of the reserve police force. We would therefore would like to know what to do with such military conscripts, especially since we know that if, of the newly invited trainees, dispatch so-and-so, some ten candidates for active policemen from our municipality have participated in a part of the training of the Croatian MUP." Have you ever seen this document before, and do you see that this professional policeman, a Muslim, fully realised that this was causing anxiety among the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to whether I've seen this specific document before, I probably have. I've seen hundreds of thousands of documents, and this is probably one of them. I agree that the document says what it says, what you've just read out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1519, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly look at D374.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that the MUP reacted to my statement quoted in "Oslobodjenje" and that this was warmongering and that I should be careful as to what I said. Now look what the executive Serbs in MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina say, and it was on the basis of their opinion and information that I reacted, and it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please indicate which part he's quoting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the interpreter's having difficulty following you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I'm going to make it simple. Can we have D374 in e-court. And I've got LiveNote instead of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We are experiencing some difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, do you know that as a rule a deputy minister is the Chief of Operations. The minister is a politician, whereas his deputy is Chief of Operations in the police force?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're speaking of the joint Bosnian MUP, I believe that's a correct assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Vitomir Zepinic was completely circumvented in the process of any decision-making, and this is this bullet which says the bypassing of the deputy minister of the police.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Vitomir Zepinic was of the opinion during the fall of 1991 that he was being circumvented in some of the decision-making - I don't know about all of the decision-making - in the joint MUP, and as a consequence of his inability or, as some thought, unwillingness to act in his capacity as deputy minister, he was increasingly also circumvented by the SDS who relied instead upon Momcilo Mandic to implement the will of the party in -- in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, speaking about the party will, Mr. Nielsen, didn't we agree on Thursday that the SDS had a task to ensure equal participation of the Serbian people and all these people had nothing to do with the party, were not related to the party in any way?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree once again that Zepinic and other Serbs such as Mandic were not members of the SDS. However, in their work, they agreed to take decisions only if those decisions were in accordance with the desires of the SDS and they consulted regularly with the leadership of the SDS before taking personnel and other decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that there were about 32 per cent of the Serbs and that the Serbian Democratic Party won over 30 per cent of the votes, of the Serbian votes, which is over 90 per cent, which made it a legitimate representative of the Serbian people in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact percentages. I do, however, believe that at the November 1990 elections, the large majority of Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina gave their votes to the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at bullet number 2, which says the abolishment of the post of the deputy undersecretary for the State Security Service which had been allocated to the SDS. Do you agree that both in democracy and in accounting, trust is based on control, and that the removal of the undersecretary for state security amounted to the hampering of the Serbian side to have any insight into the affairs relating to state security?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, and I state in paragraph 22 that, as indicated in this document, the Bosnian Serbs were very dissatisfied that this position of deputy under-secretary of the State Security Service, which had been allocated to the Serbs under the inter-party agreement, had been eliminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, look at the remaining bullet points relating to the recruiting of people who were criminally prosecuted, the inciting of empty army sentiments which is reflected in the written instruction to the MUP not to take criminal records. And look at the last bullet point. It says: "The issuance of official ID cards to the people who are not working in the MUP." Do you agree that if you have a policeman appearing with an official ID, in our system, even if he didn't have a warrant was to be allowed to have access either to individuals or premises?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that is correct at that time -- at that point in time. I would also point out since we have this document in front of us, just as it adds to a point that I made earlier that that is also a document where there is an insistence that it not -- that it is not sufficient that there be a certain number of Serbs in the MUP. They must, rather, specifically be Serbs who are not servile, that is, there is an opposition to Serbs who are being appointed without what is viewed as appropriate consultation with the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, Dr. Nielsen, we are requesting to be represented, the Serb people, to be represented by its legitimate representatives and not by puppets on string.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated in this document and in numerous intercepts during the summer and the fall of 1991, from the point of view of the SDS it was the sole legitimate representative of the Serb nation, and therefore any Serbs who did not enjoy the approval or support of that party could not be regarded as proper Serbs and indeed were regarded, as I note in paragraph 22, as servile Serbs instead, particularly in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, we have established that these people who were in the police, who had always been in the police and were not SDS members, were professional and that they are actually asking the SDS to be -- to protect them and to ensure that they have an equal status in the police. They are addressing Mr. Zepinic in that respect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated, I have included here the very important letter of Goran Zecevic to the SDS council which is, indeed, in precisely the vein that you just mentioned. I would, however, note that we do not have a sufficient number of documents to demonstrate a clear pattern that Serbs in the police were, as matter of course, asking the SDS to protect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come to that later. But now that you mentioned the intercepts from 1991, how did it happen that we have transcripts of virtually or nearly each conversation conducted by members of the Serbian leadership in Bosnia?
